l01.title: Lesson 1: The alphabet and its sounds

h-sound.title: The sound of г
h-sound.body: A voiced fricative, the voiced partner of х. Phoneticians describe it differently: /ɦ/, glottal, in the published IPA illustration (Pompino-Marschall et al. 2017); [ʕ] before а, о, у, и, е, [ɣʲ] when softened, and [ɣ] before voiced consonants and at the end of a word in Vakulenko 2025, who finds no convincing evidence for glottal [ɦ]. Both agree that it is voiced, which English h is not: Vakulenko finds English h closer to х. The plosive /ɡ/ has its own letter, ґ.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

v-allophones.title: The variants of в
v-allophones.body: One phoneme, /ʋ/, with variants by position: labiodental [ʋ] before front vowels, nearer [w] before rounded back vowels, and [u̯] at the end of a syllable, as in був (was, masculine). It does not turn into f. Vakulenko 2025 disputes the label [w], since the lips barely protrude, and writes [β̞].

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

y-vowel.title: The vowel и
y-vowel.body: Written /ɪ/ here, following the IPA illustration: retracted and lowered compared with і, with a hard consonant before it. Close to the Russian vowel [ɨ], but not the same sound. Vakulenko 2025 transcribes it as a lowered, advanced [ɨ] instead. Without stress it comes close to е.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

o-unreduced.title: о without stress
o-unreduced.body: Written /ɔ/ here, following the IPA illustration. Unlike in Russian, it does not reduce towards a without stress: вода́ is never вада́. It can still shift slightly, towards [o] before a stressed /u/. Vakulenko 2025 describes the vowel as close-mid [o] rather than /ɔ/.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

shared-forms.title: One form, several cells
shared-forms.body: Case endings overlap, so one form can fill several cells: кімнати is genitive singular and nominative, accusative and vocative plural, and кімнаті is both dative and locative singular. On this board either slip is right in any of its cells.

soft-hard.title: Soft, half-soft and hard
soft-hard.body: Only the denti-alveolars /t d n s z t͡s d͡z r l/ have a true contrast between plain and palatalized phonemes, as in лад and ладь, or рис and рись. Other consonants become half-palatalized, or "semi-soft", as a variant before /i/ and /j/. Plain consonants are velarized, which is why л is usually dark [ɫ]. The consonant before е and и stays hard.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Feldstein, An Approach to Ukrainian Reading for Russian Students

final-voicing.title: No final devoicing
final-voicing.body: Unlike Russian and most other modern Slavic languages, Ukrainian keeps a voiced consonant voiced at the end of a word: віз ends in [z], and ваз differs from вас. Assimilation mostly goes one way: a voiceless consonant becomes voiced before a voiced one, as in о́тже [ˈɔd͡ʒɛ], but a voiced one doesn't devoice before a voiceless one. The exception is г, which becomes [x] before к and т, as in легки́й and ні́гті. In fast speech a final voiced consonant can partly devoice.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA
Feldstein, An Approach to Ukrainian Reading for Russian Students

free-stress.title: Free, moving stress
free-stress.body: Stress can fall on any syllable, can tell words apart, as in доро́га and дорога́, and can move within one word's forms: роби́ти, роблю́, ро́биш. Ordinary writing doesn't mark it, so it has to be learned with each word.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

apostrophe.title: The apostrophe
apostrophe.body: It stands before я, ю, є, ї, mainly after б, п, в, м, ф, р and after a prefix ending in a consonant, when the consonant stays hard and [j] is pronounced: м'яч, п'ю, подвір'я, в'їзд. Without it, я, ю and є soften the consonant instead: ряд, люк.

one-sound-two-letters.title: Two letters, one sound
one-sound-two-letters.body: дж and дз are written with two letters but are single affricates, /d͡ʒ/ and /d͡z/: джерело, дзвін. They have no letter of their own in the alphabet.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

iotated.title: я, ю, є, ї
iotated.body: At the start of a word or after a vowel, each is [j] plus a vowel: я́блуко, моя́. After a consonant, я, ю, є soften it and write the vowel: ряд, люк. ї always stands for two sounds.

sources.title: Pompino-Marschall, Steriopolo & Żygis (2017), Ukrainian, Journal of the IPA

pronoun-n.title: н after a preposition
pronoun-n.body: After a preposition that takes the genitive or accusative, the third-person pronouns take н: його but у ньо́го, її but у не́ї, їх but у них. A preposition that takes the dative does not change them: завдяки́ йому́. The locative always has н, since it is never used without a preposition: на ньо́му, на ній, на них.

vocative.title: The vocative
vocative.body: Ukrainian has a separate form for addressing someone. Nouns in -а usually take -о (ма́мо), soft ones -е, -є or -ю (зе́мле, Марі́є, бабу́сю). Masculine nouns usually take -е (бра́те, па́не), with г changing to ж (дру́же), or -у or -ю (си́ну, учи́телю). The nominative is not used for this in careful speech.

animate-accusative.title: A person in the accusative
animate-accusative.body: A masculine noun for a person or animal has its accusative like its genitive: ба́чу бра́та. For a thing it is like the nominative: ба́чу стіл. In the plural, the same holds for people: ба́чу браті́в.

dative-ovi.title: Two forms in the dative
dative-ovi.body: Masculine nouns have two dative forms, -ові or -еві and -у or -ю: бра́тові and бра́ту are both correct. -ові is common for people. The locative of a person has -ові too, as well as -і: на бра́тові, на бра́ті. This board shows the -ові forms.

pronoun-stress.title: Stress after a preposition
pronoun-stress.body: After a preposition, мене́ and тебе́ are stressed on the first syllable: у ме́не, до те́бе. нас and вас do not change.

conjugations.title: Two conjugations
conjugations.body: Ukrainian verbs fall into two conjugations. The first has -еш or -єш in the second person singular and -уть or -ють in the third plural: пи́шеш, пи́шуть, чита́єш, чита́ють. The second has -иш or -їш, and -ать or -ять: ро́биш, ро́блять.

third-no-t.title: First conjugation: no -ть in the third singular
third-no-t.body: In the first conjugation, the third person singular ends in the vowel: чита́є, пи́ше. The second conjugation has -ть: ро́бить.

labial-l.title: л after a labial
labial-l.body: In the second conjugation, a stem ending in a labial adds л in the first person singular and in the third plural: роблю́, ро́блять, but ро́биш and ро́бить.

past-gender.title: The past agrees in gender
past-gender.body: The past tense agrees with its subject in gender and number and has no person ending: я чита́в or я чита́ла, depending on who is speaking, and ми чита́ли. The masculine usually ends in -в: чита́в. After some stems it has no ending: ніс, міг.

future-two.title: Two forms of the future
future-two.body: The imperfective future has two forms that mean the same: бу́ду чита́ти and чита́тиму. The second adds -му, -меш, -ме, -мемо, -мете, -муть to the infinitive.

name-formula.title: Asking a name
name-formula.body: Ukrainian asks how someone is called, with зва́ти or звуть and the person in the accusative: Як тебе́ зва́ти? Мене́ зва́ти Окса́на, or Мене́ звуть Окса́на. It can also use ім'я́ with a possessive: Як твоє́ ім'я́? Моє́ ім'я́ — Окса́на.

ty-vy.title: ти and ви
ty-vy.body: ви is polite as well as plural. Use it with adults you don't know well, and at work, until you are invited to change to ти: перейти́ на ти. ти is for friends, family and children.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 4: Знайомство, або Як тебе звати

no-to-be.title: No "to be" in the present
no-to-be.body: The present tense normally leaves out the verb "to be": Я студе́нт. Він з Украї́ни.

from-in.title: Where from, and where
from-in.body: з takes the genitive for where someone comes from: з Украї́ни. в or у takes the locative for where someone is: в Украї́ні, у Німе́ччині. в and у alternate to ease pronunciation, and so can з and із.

patronymic.title: Name and patronymic
patronymic.body: A respectful address uses the name and the patronymic, both in the vocative. A woman's -івна or -ївна becomes -івно or -ївно, and a man's -ович or -йович becomes -овичу or -йовичу.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 5: Привітання. Звертання. Етикетні формули

clock-time.title: Telling the time
clock-time.body: The hour is a feminine ordinal, agreeing with годи́на, even when годи́на itself is left out: Котра́ годи́на? — Тре́тя. At an hour is о with the locative: о тре́тій. Before a vowel о becomes об: об одина́дцятій. Half past names the hour ahead with на and the accusative, so 2:30 is пів на тре́тю.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 6: Час і період. Місяці

count-time.title: Counting time
count-time.body: A noun after a number changes with the number. One takes the nominative singular: одна́ годи́на. Two, three and four take the nominative plural, often with the stress of the genitive singular: дві годи́ни, дві доби́, два мі́сяці. Five and up take the genitive plural: п'ять годи́н. The last digit decides above twenty, and 11 to 14 count as many: одина́дцять годи́н.

teens-stress.title: Stress from 11 to 19
teens-stress.body: From 11 to 19 the stress falls on -на́дцять: одина́дцять, чотирна́дцять, дев'ятна́дцять.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 6: Час і період. Місяці

month-in.title: In a month
month-in.body: In a month is у or в with the locative. Most month names end in a soft consonant and lose the vowel before it: сі́чень, у сі́чні. лю́тий is an adjective in form, so it goes у лю́тому. листопа́д ends hard and goes у листопа́ді. A month name starts with a consonant, so в follows a vowel, and у follows a consonant or opens a sentence. Before в it is always у: у ве́ресні.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 6: Час і період. Місяці

season-when.title: In a season
season-when.body: In a season is usually a single adverb, with no preposition: взи́мку, навесні́, влі́тку, восени́. The first and third also begin with у: узи́мку, улі́тку. You will also hear зимо́ю, весно́ю, лі́том and о́сінню.

sources.title: Є-мова, урок 6: Час і період. Місяці
